## 2. YouTube description (the first two lines are the hook shown before “more”)

### 2.1 English (main) — 2547 characters (limit 5000)

```text
Absorbance 0.486 — which concentration is that? It depends on the calibration behind it.
In about 90 seconds: the calibration curve, and how LabGuide records the calibration.

In this video:
• How light absorbed in a photometer becomes a signal (schematic, general principle).
• Calibrators with assigned values, five illustrative points and a least-squares line: slope, intercept, R².
• Reading a control off the curve; why R² alone is not enough and what residuals should look like.
• Real LabGuide screens: instrument, analyte, reagent REF and IFU revision, the calibration record, the acceptance rule, the on-device log and its history.

Chapters
0:00 Why absorbance needs a calibration
0:17 Light path and calibrators
0:27 Curve, control and residuals
0:53 LabGuide: record the calibration
1:08 Acceptance rule, log and history

What LabGuide does today:
• LabGuide documents a calibration; it does not perform it and does not calibrate the analyzer.
• A record cannot be saved as “Accepted” until QC after calibration has passed and an approver (name or role) is entered.
• Saved records go to a calibration log stored on your device; creating, editing and deleting a record each leave a history entry.
• Without a verified guide for the instrument, LabGuide does not guess calibration parameters.

Good to know:
• The five-point straight line is an illustrative example; the number of points, the model and the acceptance limits come from your reagent IFU and your lab’s SOP.
• The app asks for an approver’s name or role; it does not verify identity or authority.
• Schematic illustration — not an exact instrument model.

LabGuide is a clinical-laboratory companion app for lab professionals and students (English, Russian, Uzbek). It is a learning and reference tool: it does not diagnose or interpret patient results. Works offline and without an account.
Get the app: [[LINK_APP_STORE]] · [[LINK_PLAY]]

Illustrative data — not patient results.
Educational use, not medical advice.
English synthetic narration (Kokoro-82M, Apache-2.0); English subtitles.
Expert review pending: this content has not yet been reviewed by a laboratory specialist.

Credits
• Narration: AI text-to-speech, Kokoro-82M v1.0 (Apache-2.0), voice af_heart, run with kokoro-onnx (MIT).
• Fonts: Inter and Instrument Serif, SIL Open Font License 1.1.
• Illustrations, schematics, animation and app screens: LabGuide (own work). No third-party photographs, stock footage, music or logos.
• Made with Remotion and FFmpeg.

#LabGuide #Calibration #ClinicalChemistry
```

* YouTube end screen (last ~7–20 s): subscribe + the next video in the SAME language edition (`qc`, `photometry`) + the playlist `[[LINK_PLAYLIST]]`. Place elements so they do not cover the end card's path pill or disclosure notices (check against the final scene).

## 11. Safe-content notes

* No patient data, names or real results anywhere. All numbers on screen are illustrative and labelled so.
* No third-party logo, brand name, stock footage or music. The only logo is the owner's app icon.
* Do not call the voice "natural", "professional" or "human": it is synthetic and nobody has listened to it yet.
* Do not call the content "approved", "verified", "certified" or "clinically validated": expert review is pending.
